notes:
v0.3.40 - nine releases in one: a Local models screen, and a launcher that stops getting in your way

This is a bigger jump than usual - everything since 0.3.31.

NEW: a "Local models" screen (/models in the sidebar). Per model it shows what
each context window actually costs in memory on YOUR PC, measured from real
loads rather than estimated, and colours each size by whether it fits your
graphics card, spills into system RAM, or will not load. It recommends a size
from your real RAM and VRAM, and shows nothing rather than guessing if it could
not read them. Reasoning and keep-alive are switchable per model. Installing and
removing models moved here from Settings.

FIXED: the agent was sending a 32k context on every local reply. On an 8 GB card
that puts about 4 GB of the model into system RAM, read back over PCIe on every
word. Four parts of the app disagreed about that number and evicted each other's
model between turns; they now agree.

FIXED: your desktop shortcut. Clicking it could open a browser tab instead of
the app, do nothing at all for five minutes after a launch, or land on a second
copy of the app installed against the wrong port. Shortcuts left pointing at
files that no longer exist are repaired on launch, and there is one desktop icon
again.

FIXED: typing a slash command sent it to the AI - /models was meant to open the
models screen and instead the agent answered by naming itself. Those places are
all buttons; the labels no longer pretend otherwise.

FIXED: Docker Desktop's window appeared for several seconds on a cold start. It
stays off screen now, unless you already had it open.

FIXED: "Turn off" for local models worked but the screen could not see that it
had, so it kept offering the same button. It now says the change takes effect on
restart.

NEW: your mouse's back and forward buttons move between screens, as do
Alt+Left/Right.

FIXED: the companion app showed Python's logo in Task Manager and the tray. It
wears the SocialAgent icon now, and updates itself with the app.

FIXED: the "Shut down everything" power emblem was a character your font had no
glyph for, so Windows substituted another font and it sat off centre - or showed
an empty box on a PC without it. It is drawn now.
